rubric.result: The objective promises two things: HeatBlock asks for coupling at the exact level heat just resolved, and it asks again every time that level changes. Both are in the diff. web/src/Heat.tsx adds a second effect that returns early while `heat === null`, then calls `fetchCoupling(repoId, window, heat?.path, signal)` — the level comes from the resolved `Heat`, not from the block's own `path` state, so it is the level heat actually resolved (which matters after a save, where `path` is `undefined` and the server re-anchors). Its dependency array `[repoId, window, heat?.path]` is what makes it fire again on every level change and on a window change, and the abort in the cleanup drops the answer of a level that was left. Nothing the objective names is missing.

The **TDD:** line asks for `it('asks coupling for the same level heat is showing')` and states the assertion: after drilling down to 'src/checkout', `urls` contains a `/api/repos/alpha/coupling?window=12m&path=src%2Fcheckout` request. web/src/Heat.test.tsx:231-247 is that test (as `test(...)`, the idiom of every other test in this file) and its body is that assertion: it renders the block, waits for the first level, clicks `row('checkout/')`, waits for `['pago/']` — so the drill-down really happened before the check — and asserts `expect(urls).toContain('/api/repos/alpha/coupling?window=12m&path=src%2Fcheckout')`. Same assertion, same input, same expected value, character for character including the `%2F` encoding, which `fetchCoupling` in web/src/api/client.ts produces via `encodeURIComponent`.

Three blocks to compare. (1) The `Call site (web/src/Heat.tsx)` block: the diff states the same two `useState` hooks with the same names and types (`coupling: Coupling | null`, `couplingError: ApiErrorCode | null`), the same guard `if (heat === null) return`, the same `setCoupling(null)`/`setCouplingError(null)` reset, the same `void loadCoupling(controller.signal)`, the same abort cleanup and the same dependency array `[repoId, window, heat?.path]`. The prose asks that `loadCoupling` mirror `loadHeat`: it does — try/catch, `if (signal.aborted) return` on both paths, `codeOf(caught)`. One wording difference: the prose writes `fetchCoupling(repoId, window, heat.path, signal)` and the diff writes `heat?.path`. Same value — `Heat.path` is a non-optional `string` in web/src/api/types.ts and the effect already returned when `heat` is null — and `?.` is what keeps the nested async function compiling, since the narrowing does not reach inside it. Not a divergence of contract. (2) The `Current state (web/src/Heat.test.tsx)` block for `stubHeat`: its signature and return shape (`{ urls: string[] }`) are unchanged; the branch is added inside. (3) The prescribed default `/coupling` answer: `emptyCouplingOf` returns `pairs: []`, `minCoOccurrences: 5`, and `mainFolder`/`fallback`/`path`/`headSha` read off the very `Heat` the same double answers for that level — exactly the four fields the brief names — plus `commits`, which the `Coupling` interface in types.ts declares as required, so a smaller object would not typecheck. The brief's clause 'unless the test overrides it' describes when the default applies; no sentence asks for an override parameter, and no test in this task passes one. Adding one would be the addition `conventions/simplicity.md` names ('which call breaks without it? Name it. If none does, it goes'), so leaving it out is the contract satisfied, not shortened.

Rows this diff bears on, one by one. 'New endpoint — GET /api/repos/:id/coupling, same query shape (window, path)': implemented with that value, both in the request the effect makes and in the URL the new test pins. 'Scope of a pair — the SAME path heatTree resolves, over the SAME window': implemented — the effect reads `heat?.path` (the level the heat answer resolved) and the same `window` prop, never a path of its own. 'Minimum co-changes MIN_CO_OCCURRENCES = 5 ... echoed in the payload as minCoOccurrences': the double's default answer carries `minCoOccurrences: 5`, the value that row states. Rows the diff leaves alone, and which therefore comply: the percent formula, the sort order, `COUPLING_ROW_LIMIT = 8`, the shape of the new server module, and where the child/main-folder decisions live — all of them server-side or UI-rendering decisions of other tasks. No row is reopened with a different value.

Exemplars: `web/src/Heat.test.tsx`'s own `stubHeat` is the double the plan told this task to extend, and the extension is in place inside it (one `level`, one `body` chosen by URL) rather than as a second double; `web/src/Heat.tsx`'s `loadHeat` effect is the exemplar the new coupling effect copies, and it copies it line for line — `AbortController`, state reset, `void load...`, `signal.aborted` guards, `codeOf`. `conventions/testing.md`: 'A double of a whole conversation answers by what it is asked, not by order' — satisfied literally, `isCouplingRequest` reads `new URL(url, 'http://test.invalid').pathname.endsWith('/coupling')`, so no branch depends on call order; the test name is the sentence, not the method. `conventions/style.md`: both files are `(modify)` paths that pre-date the document and are written throughout in free functions with docstrings, so the declared-debt exemption covers the new docstrings and the new module-level test helpers, which follow their host's idiom; the hole the same document closes does not open here, because nothing in the diff is a new concept sheltering in an old file — the coupling *load* extends the block's existing fetch idiom and the three helpers extend the double the plan named. `conventions/decisions.md`: no rule is written twice — the child/main-folder/level decision is not re-derived, the effect takes the level from the server's own answer; the `5` in `emptyCouplingOf` is fixture data of a boundary payload, not a second copy of the threshold's decision (no business change forces touching both at once, and no assertion in this task depends on its value). `conventions/simplicity.md`: one declared clash, and I leave it out of the findings for the reason item 5 gives. `coupling` and `couplingError` are written and never read — no consumer exists in this task, which is what 'a field ... answers to a call that exists' forbids — but the brief's `Call site` block prescribes both hooks verbatim, so removing them would be a `contrato` finding instead, and the reader arrives with the 'Acoplamiento' section of the slice's end state. The implementer could not satisfy both texts; the gap is the plan's task split, judged elsewhere. `conventions/boundaries.md` and `conventions/domain.md`: no adapter, port, value object or outward projection is touched — `fetchCoupling` and the `Coupling` type already existed; nothing new crosses the edge here. `conventions/defects.md`, its four rules answered one by one. Closed vocabulary: no new classifying value is held as a loose string or boolean; `aKind`/`bKind` stay the `'dir' | 'file'` of types.ts and are untouched. The `isCouplingRequest` boolean classifies a *request path* inside a test double, not a state an answer carries, and its `else` is the pre-existing heat behaviour, so it is not a catch-all over a vocabulary this diff owns. Raw map as the return value of logic: none added — `emptyCouplingOf` returns the declared `Coupling` interface, the effect stores that object, and `stubHeat` still returns `{ urls }`; `TREE`'s `Record<string, ...>` is pre-existing fixture data, not the return of logic. Two fields that have to agree: one subject, and it is the finding below — `lastHeatUrl` returns `''` for 'there is no heat request', a sentinel where `string | undefined` was available. Nothing else: `coupling`/`couplingError` are two states for two different facts (an answer, a code) and cannot disagree, and `emptyCouplingOf` derives every echoed field from the same `Heat` instead of restating it. Errors named for what happens, not for where: no error type is added; `couplingError` holds an `ApiErrorCode` produced by the existing `codeOf`, and the codes are the cause vocabulary of types.ts.

The diff has exactly one `-` line inside a test body: `expect(pathOf(urls.at(-1) ?? '')).toBeNull()` becomes `expect(pathOf(lastHeatUrl(urls))).toBeNull()` in 'choosing another main folder rescopes the percentages and is remembered'. It asserts the same thing — the reload after a save asks for no level at all, which is the sentence the comment above it states — over a request identified more precisely instead of positionally. The change is called for by this task's own **Objective:**: once coupling is asked right after heat resolves, the last URL of the run is the `/coupling` request for the re-anchored level, which carries `path=src%2Fcheckout`, so the untouched assertion would have failed for a reason its name is not about. Nothing is removed, no case is dropped, and no expectation is loosened: `lastHeatUrl` narrows the subject to the `/heat` request the assertion was always about. Every other `-` line in the diff is in a docstring, an import line or the `json:` body expression of the double — no assertion, case or test.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code. The `/coupling` request the new test observes comes from web/src/Heat.tsx's new `useEffect` calling `fetchCoupling`, and the URL string it pins is built by `fetchCoupling` in web/src/api/client.ts (`/api/repos/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/coupling?window=${window}${level}`) — neither of those lines is in the test. The test's scaffolding only answers: `stubHeat` records the URL and hands back a body, and `emptyCouplingOf` shapes that body. Revert the fourteen production lines of Heat.tsx and `urls` never gains a `/coupling` entry, so the assertion falls. The hard-coded `minCoOccurrences: 5` and `pairs: []` of the double are not asserted by anything in this task, so no expected value is met by the fixture instead of by the code.

Inside the two declared files, every line traces to a sentence of the task: the two import lines and the two `useState` hooks (asked for by name in the task's prose and its `Call site` block), the coupling effect (the `Call site` block), the URL branch of `stubHeat` plus `emptyCouplingOf` and `isCouplingRequest` (the paragraph that orders the double to branch on the pathname and answer a default empty `Coupling`), `lastHeatUrl` and the one assertion it serves (the consequence of that same change, see `manipulacion-tests`), and the new test (**TDD:**/**Tests:**). What `### Out of scope` names by name is left alone: nothing of Pulso or Gente is touched, no navigation is added or altered — the effect only observes the level the existing navigation resolves — and there is no repo-to-repo, complexity or over-time work. Also absent, correctly: any rendering of `coupling`, which the slice's end state places in the block but no sentence of this task asks for. No refactor, rename or adjacent fix rode along.

One new test, web/src/Heat.test.tsx:231-247. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no randomness, no sleep and no network — `fetch` is stubbed, the only URL base is the literal `http://test.invalid` used for parsing, and both waits are `waitFor` on rendered rows rather than on time. Isolated: it builds its own double with `stubHeat(TREE)` and web/src/testing/setup.ts runs `cleanup()` and `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` after every test, so it leaves the state it found and needs no order from the rest of the file. Verifies real behaviour: the assertion is on the literal request the production code sent through the boundary — `conventions/testing.md`'s 'At a boundary, the literal payload' — not on a call count or on a value the test defined; with the Heat.tsx lines of this diff reverted the recorded `urls` hold no `/coupling` entry and the test fails. The two `rowNames()` waits are synchronisation for the drill-down, not the subject of the assertion. All three properties hold, so I report nothing under this item, and I therefore did not need the `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` text, which the rubric requires only before reporting the finer half. The `lastHeatUrl` sentinel and the coincidental `urls.at(-1)` assertion both live in tests that already existed and are reported once, under `patrones`.

findings.what: `lastHeatUrl` answers 'there is no heat request in this run' with the empty string, a sentinel where the type could have carried the absence (`string | undefined`, which is what `Array.prototype.find` already returns). The case that shows what it costs: `new URL('', 'http://test.invalid')` has no `path` query parameter, so `expect(pathOf(lastHeatUrl(urls))).toBeNull()` also passes when the save triggered no heat reload at all — the very thing the comment above it says is being protected. It is a `low` and not a `medium` because the line it replaces carried the identical fallback (`urls.at(-1) ?? ''`), so the assertion is no weaker than before (see `manipulacion-tests`) and the fix is one signature: return the `undefined` and let the assertion name it.
findings.evidence: `return [...urls].reverse().find((url) => !isCouplingRequest(url)) ?? ''` — against `conventions/defects.md`: "A sentinel value is that second field wearing the first field's clothes. The empty string standing for \"no message\" ... The absence goes in the type, where the consumer cannot forget it."

findings.what: The new effect makes a pre-existing assertion pass for a coincidental reason. In 'going up one level asks for the parent' (untouched by this diff) the check reads whichever URL landed last, and after this task that is the `/coupling` request the level change triggers, not the `/heat` request the test's name is about; it still passes only because both requests happen to carry the same `path` today. It could still fail for the reason its name gives — a wrong parent would reach both requests — which is why this is a `low` and not a block, and the implementer declared it. The fix already exists in the same file: `lastHeatUrl`, applied here as it was applied to the save test. Worth naming because the next endpoint the block calls with a different path silently turns the check green.
findings.evidence: `expect(pathOf(urls.at(-1) ?? '')).toBe('src/checkout')`, now reached last by the diff's own `void loadCoupling(controller.signal)` — against `conventions/testing.md`: "ask whether that assertion could fail for the reason its name gives", and its antipattern "an assertion that matches loose ... when the distinctive sentence was there to use instead".
